dva-ini-061.text: An administrative endpoint of an internal application must accept only identity calls AWS authorised, signing each application with credentials IAM (SigV4). No API Gateway, what type of authorization implements this model?
options: Open access with IP validation in the Lambda
API key in the header x-api-key
Basic Auth with fixed user and password in API Gateway
Authorisation IAM (AWS_IAM), requiring signed requests with SigV4 and permissions to execute-api in the politics of the caller
dva-ini-061.explanation: With auth AWS_IAM, o API Gateway validates SigV4 signature and permissions IAM of the caller — ideal for internal APIs consumed by identities AWS (service roles, internal tools).
dva-ini-061.hint: ‘signed' requirement with credentials AWS of the caller: the mode of authorization that speaks IAM.
optionRationales: With auth AWS_IAM, o API Gateway validates SigV4 signature and permissions IAM of the caller — ideal for internal APIs consumed by identities AWS (service roles, internal tools).
API keys measure consumption and do not authenticate identities — any key holder passes.
Home IP Validation is Fragile (NAT, proxies) and late — native authorization blocks before backend.
The API Gateway does not offer native Basic Auth — and shared fixed credentials are bad practice.

dva-ini-062.text: A function Lambda You need to access a bank RDS which is in private subnets of a VPC. Which configuration allows the function to reach the bank through the private network?
options: Copy data from RDS for the S3 every hour
Configure the function to run on VPC, by associating it with sub-networks and a Security Group authorised in the SG of the RDS
Use the console of AWS as an intermediary of the desires
Return or RDS publicly accessible on the Internet
dva-ini-062.explanation: Functions connected to VPC receive ENIs in the indicated subnets and start to reach private resources; the SG of the function is then authorized in the bank's entry rule — the default path Lambda→RDS private.
dva-ini-062.hint: To talk to those who live in the private network, the function needs to 'live' there too (ENIs in VPC) — with the right SG badge.
optionRationales: Functions connected to VPC receive ENIs in the indicated subnets and start to reach private resources; the SG of the function is then authorized in the bank's entry rule — the default path Lambda→RDS private.
Exposing the bank publicly for convenience of the function reverses the security posture — the function is that it goes to the private network.
Periodic copies change the architecture and consistency — do not resolve the transactional access of the function to the bank.
The console is human interface — applications connect directly through the network with their own credentials.

dva-ini-063.text: A development team received access to the account AWS the manager asked to apply the principle of 'separation of environments' in the permissions: developers can experiment freely in the environment of dev, but in production only implant via pipeline. What is the main motivation of security of this separation?
options: Save costs, as extensive permissions are charged by AWS
Allow everyone to use root user in dev
Preventing the pipeline from having any permission in production
Reduce the risk of unaudited manual changes in production: humans have wide permissions only where the impact is low, and production changes only by automated and traceable process
dva-ini-063.explanation: Restricting production to the pipeline ensures review, audit trail and reproducibility, while freedom remains in the low-impact environment — aligned to the lowest privilege by context.
dva-ini-063.hint: Human hand looses in the playground; in production, only the robot with audit trail.
optionRationales: Restricting production to the pipeline ensures review, audit trail and reproducibility, while freedom remains in the low-impact environment — aligned to the lowest privilege by context.
Permissions IAM do not generate collection — motivation is risk control, not price.
It's the opposite: the pipeline is precisely the path authorized to change production.
Root is never a daily work tool in any environment.

dva-ini-064.text: A team wants to automate the path of the code to production: at each push in the repository, run build and tests and, if everything passes, automatically deploy. AWS orchestrate these steps in a continuous delivery flow?
options: Amazon SQS, chaining build and deploy rows
AWS CloudTrail, executing registered staff
AWS CodePipeline, defining successive connected source, build and deploy stages
AWS Trusted Advisor
dva-ini-064.explanation: The CodePipeline is the IC/CD orchestrator of AWS: detects changes in origin and conducts artifacts by stages (build, tests, approvals, deploy) automatically.
dva-ini-064.hint: The 'scanning' that links the commit to production, stage by stage.
optionRationales: The CodePipeline is the IC/CD orchestrator of AWS: detects changes in origin and conducts artifacts by stages (build, tests, approvals, deploy) automatically.
The CloudTrail records calls from API for audit — does not build or implement code.
Filas transport messages — do not run builds, tests or deployments.
The Trusted Advisor issue recommendations for good practice — is not a continuous delivery tool.

dva-ini-065.text: Within a pipeline, the step of compiling the code, running the unit tests and generating the deployment artifact needs a managed environment that executes these commands on demand, defined in a file in the repository. Which service executes this step and which file defines it?
options: AWS CodeBuild, with the commands defined in buildspec.yml
AWS Lambda, limited to builds of 15 minutes
Amazon EC2 with a built-in server turned on 24/7
AWS CodeDeploy, with the commands in appspect.yml
dva-ini-065.explanation: The CodeBuild provides ephemeral build environments on demand and performs the phases declared in buildspect.yml (install, build, artifacts) — paying only for build time.
dva-ini-065.hint: The 'builder' on demand reads your build recipe in a YAML specific at the root of the repository.
optionRationales: The CodeBuild provides ephemeral build environments on demand and performs the phases declared in buildspect.yml (install, build, artifacts) — paying only for build time.
The CodeDeploy implants artifacts in destinations (EC2, Lambda, ECS) using the app spec — the compilation and tests belong to the CodeBuild.
Permanent build server is the model that the service managed on demand replaces with less cost and maintenance.
Lambda executes application functions — is not build service with pipeline dependencies environments and cache.

dva-ini-066.text: After the build, the artifact needs to be implanted in a fleet of instances EC2, running hooks like stop the service, copy files and restart the application on each machine. Which service manages this deployment and which file describes hooks?
options: Amazon S3 with replication for the instances
AWS CodeBuild, with hooks in buildspec.yml
AWS CodeDeploy, with the implementation cycle described in appsp.yml
AWS config with implementation rules
dva-ini-066.explanation: The CodeDeploy co-ordinates implantations in EC2/on-premises, Lambda and ECS; the appsp.yml defines the files to copy and life cycle hooks (BeforeInstall, ApplicationStart etc.) in each destination.
dva-ini-066.hint: The official 'implanter' follows the app script: before installing, installing, starting, validating.
optionRationales: The CodeDeploy co-ordinates implantations in EC2/on-premises, Lambda and ECS; the appsp.yml defines the files to copy and life cycle hooks (BeforeInstall, ApplicationStart etc.) in each destination.
The CodeBuild compiles and tests — delivery on servers with life cycle hooks is the role of CodeDeploy.
The S3 store artifacts, but does not perform hooks or coordinate the implantation in machines.
Config assesses configuration compliance — does not implement applications.

dva-ini-067.text: A team evaluates implementation strategies and wants to understand the difference between rolling and blue/green. What description is correct?
options: Rolling replaces batch instances within the same environment; blue/green creates a complete new environment and exchanges traffic at once, keeping the old one for fast rollback
Rolling requires double infrastructure; blue/green updates in the same environment
Blue/green only works for databases
The two strategies bring down the whole environment during the exchange
dva-ini-067.explanation: These are the classic definitions: rolling gradually updates the existing environment (mixed capacity during the process), while blue/green parallelizes environments and switches traffic — rollback is just returning the pointer.
dva-ini-067.hint: One changes the parts of the plane in flight, gradually; the other parks a new plane next to it and transfers the passengers.
optionRationales: These are the classic definitions: rolling gradually updates the existing environment (mixed capacity during the process), while blue/green parallelizes environments and switches traffic — rollback is just returning the pointer.
It is reversed: the one who temporarily doubles the infrastructure is the blue/green; the rolling takes advantage of the current environment.
Both exist just to avoid total unavailability — gradual updating or traffic switching.
Blue/green applies to applications in general (EC2, ECS, Lambda) — banks require additional care, but are not the only target.

dva-ini-068.text: In a canary implementation of a new version of function Lambda, what is the characteristic behavior of this strategy?
options: The new version runs only in test environment, without real traffic
All traffic changes immediately to the new version
A small percentage of traffic (e.g.: 10%) goes to the new version for an observation period; if the metrics are healthy, the rest is promoted
The two versions respond together to each request and compare results
dva-ini-068.explanation: The canary exposes the novelty to a controlled slice of users such as 'sentinela': problems affect few and rollback triggers; success releases total traffic — pattern natively supported by CodeDeploy for Lambda.
dva-ini-068.hint: Like the canary in the mine: few users 'test the air' of the new version before the whole class enters.
optionRationales: The canary exposes the novelty to a controlled slice of users such as 'sentinela': problems affect few and rollback triggers; success releases total traffic — pattern natively supported by CodeDeploy for Lambda.
Total immediate exchange is all-at-once — without the partial observation period that defines the canary.
Validation without real traffic is type-approval stage — the Canary uses small-dose production traffic.
Parallel execution with comparison is shadow testing — in the canary, each request is met by UMA version according to percentage.

dva-ini-069.text: A developer has published a function Lambda and created the versions 1, 2 and 3. What is the characteristic of the numbered versions of Lambda is important for reliable implementations?
options: Published versions can be freely edited at any time
Only three versions can exist per function
Old versions are automatically deleted after 30 days
Published versions are immutable: code and configuration are frozen, ensuring that pointing to version N always executes exactly the same artifact
dva-ini-069.explanation: The immutability of the versions gives predictability to deploys and rollbacks — unlike $LATEST, which changes to each code update.
dva-ini-069.hint: Published version is revealed photograph: no one edits later — and that's a virtue for rollback.
optionRationales: The immutability of the versions gives predictability to deploys and rollbacks — unlike $LATEST, which changes to each code update.
Editable is just the $LATEST — numbered versions do not accept code change or configuration.
There is no limit of three — functions accumulate versions as published (limited by account storage)).
Versions remain explicitly excluded — do not expire alone.

dva-ini-070.text: The client application invokes a function Lambda and the team wants to change the version in production (from v3 to v4) without changing the ARN configured in the customers, and can still make the transition gradually. Lambda provides this stable pointer?
options: Ask customers to update the ARN each release
Edit Version 3 replacing the code with v4
Use $LATEST directly in production
An alias (e.g. 'prod') pointing to the current version, up-to-date and supported the traffic division between two versions
dva-ini-070.explanation: The alias is a pointer named with ARN stable: customers invoke 'prod' and the team changes destination (v3→v4) or divides traffic by weights — base of canary/linear deployments in Lambda.
dva-ini-070.hint: The fixed 'name' that customers call — and that the team repoints (or divides) under the cloths.
optionRationales: The alias is a pointer named with ARN stable: customers invoke 'prod' and the team changes destination (v3→v4) or divides traffic by weights — base of canary/linear deployments in Lambda.
Published versions are immutable — and overwriting versions would destroy the traceability of the deployee.
Linking customers to the numerical version generates fragile coordination to each employee — the alias eliminates that dependence.
$LATEST changes to each code backup — production pointed to it receives uncontrolled changes.

dva-ini-071.text: A developer prefers to define serverless infrastructure (functions, rows, tables) using a programming language like TypeScript or Python — with loops, conditions, and classes — rather than writing YAML manual. What a tool for AWS meets this preference, generating CloudFormation below?
options: AWS CloudShell
AWS Artifact
AWS CDK (Cloud Development Kit)
Amazon CodeWhisperer alone
dva-ini-071.explanation: The CDK defines infrastructure in real programming languages and 'synthesis' templates CloudFormation — combining abstracts of code (constructs) with the standard supply engine of AWS.
dva-ini-071.hint: The development kit that transforms classes and loops into templates CloudFormation.
optionRationales: The CDK defines infrastructure in real programming languages and 'synthesis' templates CloudFormation — combining abstracts of code (constructs) with the standard supply engine of AWS.
The CloudShell is a terminal in the browser — is not infrastructure framework as code.
Code assistants suggest excerpts, but it is not the framework that defines and provides the infrastructure.
The Artifact reporting compliance — no relationship with IAC.

dva-ini-072.text: No. AWS CloudFormation, What's a stack?
options: The template error log
The set of resources provided and managed as a unit from a template
The waiting line of the account's staff
A type of instance EC2 optimized for infrastructure
dva-ini-072.explanation: The stack is the living instance of the template: creation, updating and deletion act on the entire set of resources in a coordinated way, with managed state and history.
dva-ini-072.hint: The template is the plant; the 'pillar' is the building built and managed as a whole.
optionRationales: The stack is the living instance of the template: creation, updating and deletion act on the entire set of resources in a coordinated way, with managed state and history.
Stack is not running row — it's the pooling of resources provided for a template.
Stack is the concept of CloudFormation — not a hardware or family of instance.
Events and logs exist DENTRO of stack — but the stack itself is the set of resources.
